definitions.explanation: A Japanese Buddhist festival to honor the spirits of ancestors, typically held in mid-August.

examples.japanese: お{盆|ぼん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{故郷|ふるさと}→故郷：25466_furusato⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{帰|かえ}る→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧。
examples.english: I return to my hometown during Obon.

examples.japanese: お{盆|ぼん}⟦{休|やす}み→休み：02266_yasumi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{旅行|りょこう}→旅行：00748_ryokou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I travel during the Obon holiday.

examples.japanese: お{盆|ぼん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{先祖|せんぞ}→先祖：04040_senzo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{霊|れい}→霊：14667_rei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{迎|むか}える→迎える：01193_mukaeru⟧⟦{行事|ぎょうじ}→行事：00078_gyouji⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: Obon is an event to welcome the spirits of ancestors.

notes:
お{盆|ぼん} (Obon) is one of Japan's three major holiday periods, along with ⟦{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧ (New Year) and ⟦ゴールデンウィーク→ゴールデンウィーク：22760_goorudenwiiku⟧ (Golden Week). It is a Buddhist festival honoring ancestral spirits.

TIMING:
Most of Japan observes Obon from August 13-16. Some regions (notably Tokyo) observe it in mid-July. Many companies give employees {盆|ぼん}⟦{休|やす}み→休み：02266_yasumi⟧ (Obon vacation).

CULTURAL TRADITIONS:
- ⟦{迎|むか}え{火|び}→迎え火：28983_mukaebi⟧: welcoming fire (to guide spirits home)
- ⟦{送|おく}り{火|び}→送り火：14488_okuribi⟧: sending fire (to see spirits off)
- ⟦{墓参|はかまい}り→墓参り：10663_hakamairi⟧: visiting family graves
- ⟦{盆踊|ぼんおど}り→盆踊り：05638_bonodori⟧: Bon dance (community festival dance)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- お{盆|ぼん}⟦{休|やす}み→休み：02266_yasumi⟧: Obon holiday/vacation
- お{盆|ぼん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{帰省|きせい}→帰省：12419_kisei⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to return to one's hometown for Obon
